newsitem.title: USA: Equisure denies improper trading allegations.
newsitem.headline: Equisure denies improper trading allegations.

text.p: Equisure Inc said Friday it denied allegations of improper trading of its shares, trading of which was halted on August 4 by the American Stock Exchange.

Equisure said its board of directors believes the suspension resulted from allegations of improper trading activity by affiliates of Equisure. It said the board "categorically and emphatically" denies these allegations.

"We are concerned about rumors which appear to stem from unnamed sources within ASE (American Stock Exchange) and which have been noted in recent news articles," the Equisure board said in a statement. "These rumors have done great damage to the company and its shareholders."
Equisure said it is cooperating fully with the American Stock Exchange and expects to resolve this matter as soon as possible in order to prevent further damage.
The board said it is working with independent auditors to review all allegations.

Equisure, through its wholly owned subsidiary Equihot Herverzekering NV, is a reinsurance company engaged primarily in covering the financial and political risks associated with the delivery and warehousing of raw, refined or constructed metal products.
The company, based in Antwerp, Belgium, and Minneapolis, also has begun underwriting a general reinsurance account, which focuses on aviation and marine coverage but is expanding into other areas.
